title: Avenanthramide C From Oats Possibly Exerts Anti-Inflammatory Effects in Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells.
authors: Sasaki, Hiroyuki; Masutomi, Hirofumi; Nagasawa, Hajime; Matsumoto, Yuma; Okuma, Teruyuki; Otsuka, Tomoyuki; Ishihara, Katsuyuki; Suzuki, Yusuke; Ueda, Seiji
one_liner_zh: 该文研究燕麦来源的avenanthramide C抑制尿毒症毒素诱导的内皮炎症，涉及AhR对接模拟但非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with inflammation and cardiovascular complications and is partly exacerbated by the uremic toxin indoxyl sulfate (IS). IS is known to activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) to promote vascular inflammation. On the other hand, avenanthramide C (Ave), an oat-derived polyphenol, has antioxidative and anti-inflammatory properties. Therefore, we investigated whether Ave can suppress IS-induced inflammatory responses. Analysis of serum from hemodialysis patients revealed a significant correlation between IS and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels. In human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), IS (>/=50 microg/mL) increased IL-6 secretion, while Ave (>/=10 microM) suppressed this effect. Docking simulations and in vitro experiments suggested that Ave may interact with AhR and suppress IS-induced expression of AhR target genes, including that of cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1. High-performance liquid chromatography verified the uptake of Ave by human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Additionally, the anti-inflammatory effects of Ave were independent of the adrenergic alpha1 receptor, adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase pathways, and protein kinase B pathways. Ave suppresses IS-induced inflammation, thereby reducing IL-6 secretion in HUVECs. These findings suggest the potential of Ave as a dietary intervention for mitigating vascular inflammation in patients with CKD.
abstract_zh: 慢性肾脏病（CKD）与炎症和心血管并发症相关，并部分由尿毒症毒素硫酸吲哚酚（IS）加剧。已知IS可激活芳香烃受体（AhR）以促进血管炎症。另一方面，燕麦来源的多酚类化合物燕麦蒽酰胺C（Ave）具有抗氧化和抗炎特性。因此，我们研究了Ave是否能抑制IS诱导的炎症反应。对血液透析患者血清的分析显示，IS与白细胞介素-6（IL-6）水平之间存在显著相关性。在人脐静脉内皮细胞（HUVECs）中，IS（≥50微克/毫升）增加IL-6分泌，而Ave（≥10微摩尔）抑制了此效应。对接模拟和体外实验提示，Ave可能与AhR相互作用，并抑制IS诱导的AhR靶基因表达，包括细胞色素P450家族1亚家族A成员1。高效液相色谱法验证了人脐静脉内皮细胞对Ave的摄取。此外，Ave的抗炎作用独立于肾上腺素能α1受体、腺苷酸活化蛋白激酶通路和蛋白激酶B通路。Ave抑制IS诱导的炎症，从而减少HUVECs中IL-6的分泌。这些发现提示Ave作为饮食干预措施在缓解CKD患者血管炎症方面的潜力。
